vBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-1491: metric-aware flywheel prioritization — weight substrate-bug suggestions by which v1.0 criterion they affect

plan.title: feat(flywheel): metric-aware prioritization — weight substrate-bug suggestions by which v1.0 criterion they affect
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: The flywheel ranks suggestions by P-level + age only (roles/flywheel.md:225-233). All substrate bugs bucket the same; there is no signal about which bug is closest to a v1.0 criterion threshold. #1487 (PR #1505, merged) shipped the telemetry that knows which criterion is under threat; nothing consumes it for ranking. Commit 74403b36a6 landed substrate-first bucketing and explicitly left 'deterministic label-weighting in code' to this issue. NOTE: the June 2026 implementation (PR #1636) was RETIRED (closed, not merged) because it was built against the pre-remodel/pre-rebrand foundation; this is a rebuild against current code.
narratives.Proposal: Add a deterministic metric-drift weight for substrate bugs, consumed as a ranking signal by the LLM orchestrator (which authors suggestions) and surfaced in the dashboard. (1) Substrate bugs declare affected criteria via a `Flywheel-Affects-Criterion: N,M` body trailer (primary) or `affects-criterion-N` labels (parse-only fallback). (2) A pure lib computes weight+reason from affected criteria and the live 30-day stats snapshot. (3) A shared lib service joins bugs+stats+weights into a sorted table; both a new HTTP route and a new sandbox-safe CLI call it. (4) roles/flywheel.md teaches the orchestrator to call `pan flywheel weights --json` each tick and write weight/weightReason onto emitted substrate suggestions (contract extended with two optional fields). (5) The dashboard renders a weight badge + reason and applies weight as a secondary sort within an equal priority tier. Weight formula: contribution(c)=STATUS_MULT[status]*(STATUS_FLOOR[status]+normalizedDistance(c)), weight=Σ over affected criteria; STATUS_MULT {red:3,yellow:2,green:1,insufficient_data:0}, STATUS_FLOOR {red:1,yellow:0.5,green:0,insufficient_data:0}.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Non-substrate (user-pipeline) bug prioritization — those keep normal P-level ranking.
- Operator-filed / operator-injected issues always-on-top — preserved; weighting is a default sort, not a filter (NFR-1).
- Changing how the seven criteria are computed or their targets — #1487 owns that.
- Introducing per-criterion weight constants or altering the v1.0 AND-gate definition.
- Historical backfill of Flywheel-Affects-Criterion on pre-existing substrate bugs.
- Creating affects-criterion-N GitHub labels as infrastructure — labels are parse-only if present; the trailer is the primary path.
- Re-sorting a server-built suggestion list — suggestions are LLM-authored, not server-computed.

autoDecisions.summary: Mapping mechanism = `Flywheel-Affects-Criterion: N,M` body trailer (primary) + `affects-criterion-N` labels (parse-only fallback).
autoDecisions.rationale: Reuses #1487's trailer convention and substrate-bug-poller.ts parsing style; requires no GitHub label infrastructure. Issue Scope item listed both label and trailer as options; trailer is the smallest-footprint choice consistent with existing provenance.

autoDecisions.summary: Weight = Σ STATUS_MULT[status] * (STATUS_FLOOR[status] + normalizedDistance) over affected criteria.
autoDecisions.rationale: Status floor guarantees red > yellow > green ordering even when a compound criterion value (c4/c6) cannot be cleanly normalized to a scalar; the drift term still differentiates within a status. Improves on the earlier raw-distance formula which would zero-out un-normalizable criteria.

autoDecisions.summary: Criterion weights are uniform (all seven equal).
autoDecisions.rationale: Telemetry defines no per-criterion weight constants and vision.mdx treats the seven as an equal AND-gate; inventing weights would exceed scope.

autoDecisions.summary: Weight is a secondary sort WITHIN an equal priority tier; never overrides P0/urgent; never a hard filter.
autoDecisions.rationale: Issue Scope: 'metric weighting is a default sort, not a hard filter'; Out-of-scope: operator escape hatch preserved.

autoDecisions.summary: `pan flywheel weights` reads the shared lib service directly (no HTTP).
autoDecisions.rationale: The flywheel orchestrator runs in a sandbox that may not reach the dashboard HTTP port; matches the existing `flywheel merge-blockers` direct-SQLite sandbox-safe pattern in flywheel-surfaces.ts.
Before 3 completed pipeline runs in the window telemetry has no signal; ranking on noise would mislead. This is correct restraint, not a bug.

Add parseAffectedCriteria(body, labels) → number[]

narrative.Action: Create a pure function `parseAffectedCriteria(body: string | null | undefined, labels: readonly string[] = []): number[]` in a new file src/lib/overdeck/affected-criteria.ts. Parse a `Flywheel-Affects-Criterion:` trailer line (multiline, case-insensitive) whose value is a comma/space-separated list of integers, mirroring the regex style of parseSubstrateBugTrailer in src/dashboard/server/services/substrate-bug-poller.ts:105-115. ALSO parse labels matching /^affects-criterion-(\d+)$/. Union the two sources, keep only integers 1..7, dedupe, sort ascending. Return [] when neither source declares anything (must NOT require any #1487 trailer to be present). No network/DB access.

items.title: Given a body containing `Flywheel-Affects-Criterion: 1,5`, returns [1,5]; given `Affects-Criterion: 5 1 5` (any case, repeats, spaces) returns [1,5]
Given labels ['affects-criterion-3','substrate'] and no trailer, returns [3]; given both a trailer (1) and a label (3), returns the sorted union [1,3]
Rejects out-of-range values: `Flywheel-Affects-Criterion: 0,8,3` returns [3]
Given null/empty body and no labels, returns []; given a body carrying only other Flywheel trailers (Flywheel-Run-Id/Filed-By) returns []
Add computeSubstrateBugWeight(criteria, stats) → { weight, reason }

expected_outputs: substrate-bug-weight.test.ts passes with cases for each criterion type incl compound and insufficient_data

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/overdeck/substrate-bug-weight.ts exporting: (a) a `CRITERION_META` table mapping each criterion number 1..7 to { key: keyof FlywheelStatsCriteria, direction: 'lower'|'higher'|'zero', valueField?: string } per the PRD table (c4 valueField 'medianMs', c6 valueField 'ratio', c2 direction 'zero', c3 direction 'higher', rest 'lower'); (b) `computeSubstrateBugWeight(criteria: number[], stats: FlywheelStats): { weight: number; reason: string }`. For each affected criterion read stats.criteria[key]. Compute normalizedDistance: 'lower' = max(0,(value-target)/target); 'higher' = max(0,(target-value)/target); 'zero' = value. If value/target are objects, read the numeric valueField sub-field; if absent or non-numeric, normalizedDistance = 0. contribution = STATUS_MULT[status] * (STATUS_FLOOR[status] + normalizedDistance) with STATUS_MULT {red:3,yellow:2,green:1,insufficient_data:0} and STATUS_FLOOR {red:1,yellow:0.5,green:0,insufficient_data:0}. weight = Σ contributions, rounded to 2 decimals. reason describes the single highest-contribution criterion using its label + status + value/target (e.g. 'criterion 1 (substrate-bug discovery rate) red at 3.2% vs target <2%'). Empty criteria → { weight: 0, reason: 'no affected criteria declared' }. IMPLEMENTATION CHECKPOINT: confirm c4/c6 compound sub-field names by reading computeMttrCriterion/computeCriterion6Bucket in src/dashboard/server/services/flywheel-telemetry.ts (planning-verified: c4 {medianMs,p95Ms}; c6 bucket {medianMs,p95Ms,ratio}).

items.title: computeSubstrateBugWeight([1], stats) returns weight 4.8 when criterion 1 is red with value 0.032 vs target 0.02 (3*(1+0.6))
computeSubstrateBugWeight returns a larger weight for a single red criterion than for a single green criterion carrying larger raw drift (status multiplier and floor dominate)

For c4 with compound value {medianMs,p95Ms} the function returns a finite (non-NaN) weight by reading medianMs; when the configured valueField is absent it returns a weight using normalizedDistance 0 plus the status floor
computeSubstrateBugWeight over only insufficient_data criteria returns weight 0 and a reason mentioning insufficient telemetry
computeSubstrateBugWeight returns a reason string naming the highest-contributing criterion by label, status, and value-vs-target
Add listSubstrateBugWeights(window) lib service joining bugs + stats + weights

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/overdeck/substrate-bug-weights-service.ts exporting `async function listSubstrateBugWeights(window = '30d', deps?): Promise<WeightedSubstrateBug[]>`. Steps: (1) compute the window bounds and call computeFlywheelStats(window, ...inputs) — reuse the same input-derivation the route uses (see getFlywheelStatsPayload in src/dashboard/server/routes/flywheel.ts:423 which composes derivePipelineRunStatsInputs + listInWindow). (2) list in-window substrate bugs via listInWindow(since, until) from src/lib/overdeck/flywheel-substrate-bugs.ts:157. (3) for each bug, fetch its issue body+labels (bugs carry issueId; reuse whatever body source #1487 stores, else GitHub fetch is out of scope — parse from the stored row/body if available), call parseAffectedCriteria, then computeSubstrateBugWeight(criteria, stats). (4) return WeightedSubstrateBug[] = { issueId, severity, filedBy, affectedCriteria, weight, weightReason } sorted by weight desc, then filed_at asc. Inject stats/bugs via a deps param so tests avoid real DB/telemetry. Keep this the SINGLE source both the route (b5) and CLI (b6) call.
